title: Sports radio to try in Malta
intro: Radio snapshot for 13–19 October 2026. The clearest English-language sports lead is a “Sports Channel” service that one specialist directory labels “(Talk Sport)” on block 6C (185.360 MHz) while the industry multiplex table places a service of that name on block 12A and the operator’s own list shows none — block disputed, scan by name: talkSPORT is an official Premier League audio broadcaster, so this is the first receiver scan to try on 17–18 October 2026. What the Malta relay actually carries, and its indoor reception, are unverified. Malta’s block 6A carries BBC World Service (Sportsworld, dated 17–18 October episodes, general live sport) plus Rai Radio Uno/Due/Tre, NET FM and Vibe HD; Vibe FM is the published radio partner of the Malta Premier League. The six BBC Radio 5 Live / 5 Sports Extra episode JSON records name seven UK Premier League commentaries across 17–18 October (including Bournemouth–Sunderland on 5 Sports Extra 2), with individual broadcast labels distinguished from the parent programme service — still UK-only schedule evidence. Kalshi’s own help centre says trading from many countries and while travelling abroad is possible subject to its Member Agreement, while third-party guidance conflicts; eligibility stays account-specific. No named-event carriage was verified. Refreshed 11 October 2026: BBC now lists named Premier League commentaries for 17–18 October on Radio 5 Live and 5 Sports Extra, with the parent programme and individual broadcast service distinguished; those remain UK schedules, not Malta reception.

records.description: NET FM is listed by the Broadcasting Authority at FM 101 MHz, and the station’s own schedule page was read in full on 11 October 2026. It publishes three weekend sports-branded slots: Friday 18:30 “Mhux Premier biss” (“Not just the Premier League”), Saturday 16:00 “Hits & Score” and Sunday 15:00 “Sports Box”. The Saturday and Sunday slots coincide exactly with the Malta-time kick-off windows of the Premier League fixtures scheduled that weekend (most Saturday 16:00 and Sunday 15:00 fixtures), which is a testable planning lead — but the station publishes only a recurring weekly grid, with no dated 17–18 October running order and no promise of live commentary on any named match. Programmes and continuity are largely in Maltese. The grid does not state a time zone explicitly; Malta local time is the reasonable reading and the station broadcasts locally.

NET FM is also listed as a DAB+ channel by the Malta DAB+ operator: https://dab.com.mt/channels/ . The listener should recheck the station’s live page on 16–18 October: a recurring grid is not a dated schedule and the sports slots may be discussion programming rather than commentary. No on-location reception test was possible. The station also offers an internet stream, which is not broadcast radio. Second-session additions: the station is also carried on Malta DAB+ block 6A (181.936 MHz) under the service name “Net FM”, per the specialist station list read 11 October 2026: https://radioinmalta.com/en/dab/6a.php — a second tuning route if the FM signal is weak indoors. No carriage of the Thunderpick event, the Gżira United–Mosta fixture or the Rolex Middle Sea Race was confirmed. The grid does not state its time zone.

records.description: Malta has used DAB+ (not older DAB) since 2008, with national coverage from the Digi B Network multiplexes on blocks 6A, 6C and 12A, so a DAB+-compatible receiver is required and should find the services by name rather than by dial frequency. Practical split for this trip: block 6A carries BBC World Service, Rai Radio Uno/Due/Tre, Net FM, Vibe HD and most Maltese services; block 6C carries UK relays such as LBC 97.3, Capital, Gold, Smooth and Jazz FM plus several Italian services, and the specialist directory also lists a “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)” there — though the industry multiplex table places a “Sports Channel” on block 12A instead, and the operator’s own channel list shows no sports service, so scan both blocks. A one-touch scan of the three blocks is the fastest way to answer the radio question in Malta itself.

Corroborated by WorldDAB’s Malta country page and multiplex table (multiplexes operated by Digi B Network; coverage via 6A/6C/12A): https://www.worlddab.org/countries/malta and https://www.worlddab.org/countries/malta/multiplexes , and by the MCA’s DAB+ consultation frequency table: https://www.mca.org.mt/sites/default/files/MCA-C-21-4261%20-%20DAB%20Plus%20Consultation_0.pdf . Radio in Malta is a specialist enthusiast directory and WorldDAB is an industry association, so both are directory evidence, not the Maltese network operator’s live data: service names, bit rates and block contents can change, and reception inside a seafront hotel or a metal-framed studio building was not measured. records.name: What radio hardware actually works in Malta (US traveller)
records.area: Malta — national FM and DAB+ coverage
records.hours: Check before departure; a receiver bought locally removes the codec risk
records.price range: Not published here; local receiver prices were not checked
records.description: Three separate compatibility questions decide what a US traveller can actually listen to. 1) Analog FM travels: Maltese national FM stations sit inside the international FM broadcast band, which the ITU GE84 plan sets at 87.5–108 MHz for Region 1. Check the tuning range printed on any receiver before relying on it, and remember most phone radios are disabled. 2) DAB+ is not what US equipment decodes: the United States adopted HD Radio, a different digital standard, and DAB/DAB+ receivers and HD Radio receivers cannot decode each other’s signals. The BBC’s own guidance adds that even UK DAB radios will not work in Malta because of a different codec, and that a DAB+ radio purchased in Malta is the correct device. 3) A phone app or web stream is not broadcast radio: it depends on mobile data, roaming cost and any territory limits, and it should not be counted as an over-the-air radio option.
records.notes: BBC institutional listening page (Malta DAB+ carriage and the “DAB+ radio purchased in Malta is necessary… UK DAB radios operate on a different codec” wording): https://www.bbc.co.uk/worldservice/mobile/institutional/2009/03/000000_digitallisting.shtml . ITU workshop material giving the Region 1 FM broadcast band as 87.5–108 MHz under the GE84 Agreement: https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-R/terrestrial/workshops/SRME-19/Documents/Workshop/SRME-19-DigitalRadio.pdf . Encyclopaedia reference for the HD Radio/DAB+ incompatibility: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HD_Radio . WorldDAB Malta multiplexes: https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes . The third point is a practical caution, not a sourced claim about a specific app. No receiver was tested in Malta.

records.name: “Sports Channel” on Malta DAB+ — directory conflict on which block carries it
records.area: Malta DAB+; the specialist directory lists the service on block 6C (185.360 MHz) while the industry multiplex table lists a “Sports Channel” on block 12A (223.936 MHz). Reception at AX ODYCY and the Ta’ Qali venue not tested.
records.address: Not applicable — broadcast-service directory lead; scan 6A, 6C and 12A by service name, then verify the actual block and content.
records.hours: No programme schedule was found for this service, so no trip-week sports lineup can be stated. If it is the talkSPORT relay, its UK output would include the Saturday 12:30 Premier League commentary slot.
records.price range: Free-to-air if broadcast; DAB+ receiver required (hardware price not checked)
records.description: Published directories list a service called “Sports Channel” but do not agree on its block or identity. Radio in Malta labels its 6C (185.360 MHz) entry “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)”; 2025 scanner-directory observations also place a service called Sports Channel on 185.360 MHz / 6C. WorldDAB's Malta table lists a generic “Sports Channel” on Digi B 2 / 12A, while the Maltese DAB+ operator's own channel list shows no sports service. Wikipedia separately lists talkSPORT on 6C. This makes 6C the better-corroborated scan lead, not proof of current operator carriage, talkSPORT identity, local reception or live Premier League commentary. talkSPORT's UK rights are separate evidence. Scan by service name on 6C and 12A and listen before trusting the label.
records.notes: Read 11 October 2026. Two directories disagree on the block. WorldDAB’s Malta multiplex page https://www.worlddab.org/why-dab-plus/countries/malta/multiplexes lists a regular DAB+ service named “Sports Channel” on Digi B 2, transmitted on Band III 12A at 223.936 MHz, and separately lists a third multiplex Digi B 3 on Band III 6C at 185.360 MHz without a Sports Channel entry. The third-party directory Radio in Malta https://radioinmalta.com/en/stations/ describes “Talk Sport · Sports coverage and sports talk · DAB+ (Labelled as Sports Channel) · Malta · talksport.com · United Kingdom (English)” and its 6C page places the service on 6C. So the service name is corroborated but the block is disputed, and the talkSPORT identification rests only on the third-party directory — not on a broadcaster or rights-holder statement. TalkSPORT’s own schedule page https://talksport.com/schedule/ returned “Sorry, page unavailable” when checked, so no dated lineup could be confirmed. Action: scan a DAB+ receiver at AX ODYCY across both 12A and 6C for a service named “Sports Channel” and note the actual programme identity. PR #40's parallel read added technical corroboration, folded in here rather than duplicated as a second record: Radio in Malta's block 6C ensemble listing gives “Sports Channel (Talk Sport)” at 185.360 MHz with station ID C02F, 32 kbit/s DAB+ stereo HE-AAC v2; a scanner log at https://www.digitalbitrate.com/dtv.php?mux=9A&liste=2&live=623&lang=en (scanner “MALTA”, last update 20/08/2025) lists Sports Channel under “Freq : 185.360MHz”; and https://www.wohnort.org/dab/malta.html (observations 19.01.2025) lists “Sports Channel C02F” in the same C02x-series group as Radio Sportiva C02A, Magic C02B, Vatican Radio C02C and Radju Malta 2 C02D. That session also observed that WorldDAB's table contains entries named “6c_Test7” and “6c Test12”, suggesting its two tables are mis-assigned, and judged that the weight of scan evidence favours 6C. This record keeps the conflict open rather than resolving it, because no operator statement or reception test settles it; scan 6A, 6C and 12A and listen.
